title: Choose the editor-focused arrangement
question: Which editor-led layout feels most like a focused Neovim workbench while staying clear and touch-friendly on mobile?

options.label: Editor-led split
options.thesis: Keep the file tree close, but give the note roughly four-fifths of the desktop workspace and the visual emphasis.
options.viewport: Desktop: compact workspace header, restrained file tree at left, wide centered editor, and a slim Vim-style statusline. Mobile: editor-first, labeled browse and note actions, drawer navigation, and no Vim mode indicator or keyboard-only actions.
options.risk: The compact file tree must remain legible without competing with the note.

options.label: Focus canvas with browser drawer
options.thesis: Let the editor fill the workbench; bring the file tree in as a reversible side drawer when navigation is needed.
options.viewport: Desktop: a full-width writing canvas with a compact header and a labeled Browse action opening the same file tree in a side drawer. Mobile: the same canvas and drawer, with touch-sized Browse and Create actions; no Vim mode UI.
options.risk: Opening the drawer adds a step when switching notes often.

options.label: Narrow navigator split
options.thesis: Keep navigation always visible in a narrow tree while setting the editor’s measure and scale as the dominant surface.
options.viewport: Desktop: a narrow file tree, wide writing canvas, full-width workspace header, and compact statusline. Mobile: hide the tree into a labeled drawer and replace keyboard-specific status with touch actions.
options.risk: A permanent tree still takes space from small laptop viewports.
